title: From idea to architecture
summary: Turn a question about code into a diagram that explains it at a glance, faster than reading files. Topocode supplies source evidence and checks; the agent turns that evidence into a clear visual explanation; you review and refine it. This is the product's collaboration loop, not a command-by-command setup or Git procedure. Scan is useful here but not required for authored stories.

sections.title: You
sections.body: Set the question and scope. Review meaning, accuracy, and usefulness. Feedback starts another iteration; your approval, not a green check, accepts the architecture document.

sections.title: Coding agent
sections.body: Read code and scan evidence, identify what matters, and author an anchored story that explains the code visually. Repair diagnostics and preserve story identity as the explanation evolves. Present the diagram so the user can understand responsibilities and relationships without first reading every file. Interpretation here does not require the separate topo enrich command.

sections.title: Topocode CLI
sections.body: Initialize and optionally scan the repository without calling a model. Validate drafts and render committed stories. serve supplies a local viewer; bundle supplies static files. These are separate invocations across the collaboration cycle, not one long-running call.

sections.title: Repository
sections.body: Holds source code, configuration, and authored stories. The agent writes the explanation; the CLI reads source and generates the diagram. Source-backed stories are durable, while generated cache/output is disposable. This is a repository boundary, not a separate hosted service.
